intro: This page is the board and toolchain matrix. It is taken from `config/core-recipes.toml`, `config/core-library.toml`, `profiles/native-integration-dev.toml`, the per-core `toolchain.lock` files, the misteross producers, and the docs those files point at. A cell that is not in those sources is marked unverified or TBD.

The bootstrap image installs `fes.menu` and the pinned splash bitstream. Every playable core is a catalog install. Library standing `supported` is not a claim that the current bitstream has kit acceptance. Dated notes under `docs/validation/` accept only the artifact they name.

The tier names below follow the tree. They do not use "HIL-verified and shipped in the default image" as Tier 1, because no playable core is in that image and kit notes do not move forward onto a new bitstream.

tiers.label: Firmware
tiers.meaning: Board bitstream required by boot or the kit UI. `fes.menu` is the only package in the default image profile. Splash is the pinned idle RBF, not a play package.

tiers.label: Tier 1 — Catalog supported
tiers.meaning: `standing = supported` in `config/core-library.toml`, with a recipe row. Installed from the catalog. Not in the bootstrap image. This is the library's own word, not a current-byte hardware acceptance.

tiers.label: Tier 2 — Optional
tiers.meaning: Recipe `optional = true`. Today only `fes.atari-st`. Its library standing is still `experimental`. The default profile does not select it. When a selection includes it, `FES_SKIP_OPTIONAL_CORES=1` or `FES_SKIP_CORES=fes.atari-st` skips place-and-route, and `FES_REQUIRE_ALL_CORES=1` makes the omission fail the build.

tiers.label: Tier 3 — Experimental
tiers.meaning: `standing = experimental` in `config/core-library.toml`. Registered for `make core-dev` and the catalog. Not in the bootstrap image. Bring-up evidence, where it exists, is package-specific.

tiers.label: Reference
tiers.meaning: A producer or simulation module exists and core docs say it is not a registered play package. No recipe row.

tiers.label: Bring-up
tiers.meaning: A core directory with RTL and a simulation or diagnostic route, and no recipe row. Not a catalog package.

tiers.label: Shared RTL
tiers.meaning: A CPU other cores instantiate. Not a system package and not a board bitstream of its own.

tiers.label: Planned
tiers.meaning: Named future work with no core directory. No row uses this tier. DE25-Nano is a missing board shell on every row, not a core.

policy: Labels follow the accepted Quartus policy in [Quartus-built cores](design/quartus-cores.md) (issue #1163). `oss` is the Debian-style main set: Yosys + nextpnr-mistral. `quartus` is the non-free set: a proprietary toolchain. A core build is supposed to say which one made it, so an all-OSS selection can exclude every Quartus build. `FES_OSS_ONLY` is not implemented. Current registered recipes and package selection build the OSS lane only. A failed OSS route never falls back to Quartus.

Both labelled builds ship only when the published rule is met, on the same RTL and the same target clocks. Either every Quartus sign-off seed closes a required clock that an OSS sign-off seed misses, or the best complete-seed Fmax is at least 15% higher on any required clock: `100 × (Quartus best − OSS best) / OSS best`. Otherwise the core ships OSS only. No registered recipe declares a `toolchains` list yet, so no core ships both builds today. The i386 far-transfer numbers are the policy's worked example (about 40%), and they are still an oracle, not a product variant.

DE25-Nano uses an Agilex 5 device. There is no `sources/misteross/boards/de25nano` directory. nextpnr-mistral targets Cyclone V (`5CSEBA6U23I7` in [the DE10-Nano board note](../sources/misteross/boards/de10nano/README.md)). The policy says the first DE25 shells are Quartus-only, because the device is not OSS-reverse-engineered, and that Quartus Pro 24.1 or later is the first release that supports Agilex 5. No per-core DE25 recipe exists.

i386, pc386 and PC/XT are not labelled Quartus-primary in this tree. i386's Quartus 17.0.2 fit is an oracle on the same Yosys netlist, and a gap that only nextpnr shows is filed against that flow ([i386 CPU design](../sources/misteross/docs/i386-cpu-design.md)). pc386 has no sealed producer. PC/XT's producer is the OSS diagnostic, and Quartus is the cross-check that rejected an earlier nextpnr-only pass. Treating Quartus as the primary product toolchain, with nextpnr advisory, is unverified.

ColecoVision's factory recipe is the format-4 ROM map, not the blob/blob-stream mailboxes still present on the older Coleco producers. A household title count of 0 and a low-priority ranking are not stated in the tree. See the Coleco row and the unverified list.

cores.label: `fes.menu`
cores.router: Recipe `gpu_router` is HIP. This producer accepts `--gpu-device` only; the authenticated toolchain sets the backend (misteross AGENTS.md).
cores.quartus: Recipe `quartus_role` is `no oracle required`. No Quartus product variant is selected. A failed OSS route does not fall back to Quartus.
cores.features: Media: none. Input: none in the package interfaces. HDMI: fixed 720p60 menu display and blitter over HPS DDR (`fes.video.menu-display`, `fes.video.menu-blitter`). Mesh/Bluetooth: per-core unverified (host evdev and FogCast only).
cores.notes: Bootstrap image display firmware, not a playable core. The only `fpga_packages` row in `profiles/native-integration-dev.toml`. Lock nextpnr `1eecf877`. `docs/core-alignment.md` still groups menu with repository-level nextpnr `9128800f`; this matrix follows the lock file.

cores.label: splash / idle

cores.quartus: No Quartus product lane was found. The image pins `sealed/fes-splash.rbf` for U-Boot `/idle.rbf` and Stop idle.
cores.features: Media: none. Input: none. No MiSTer user-io (Probe `0x0014` and HPS framebuffer `0x002f` are unanswered). HDMI: 720p60 logo. Mesh/Bluetooth: per-core unverified (host evdev and FogCast only).
cores.notes: Board firmware, not a `fes.*` recipe and not in `config/core-library.toml`. Not a play package.

cores.label: `fes.coleco`
cores.router: Recipe `gpu_router` is HIP. This producer accepts `--gpu-router HIP` or `CUDA` (misteross AGENTS.md).

cores.features: Media: format-4 ROM map, exact 8 KiB `coleco-bios` plus 16 KiB `coleco-cart`. The recipe producer strips `fes.media.blob`, `fes.media.blob-stream` and `fes.firmware.blob`. No live media unit. Guide Change media relaunches the same title with another exact-size `.col`/`.rom`/`.bin` (`POST /api/v1/session/cartridge`); the saved cartridge binding is unchanged. Input: `fes.gamepad.ports` and `fes.keypad.ports`. HDMI: native-pixel shell, mandatory Direct or Scanlines part, then the session display plane, fixed 720p60. CPU: TV80, not `fes_z80_nmos`. Mesh/Bluetooth: per-core unverified (host evdev and FogCast only).
cores.notes: Library standing `supported`. Not retail-complete. The `example.coleco-arcade` room names five cabinets and skips any that are not installed; an empty library shows `no Coleco arcade titles in this library yet`. A committed title count of 0 and a low-priority ranking were not found (unverified). Older `build_fes_coleco.py` and `build_fes_coleco_oss.py` still declare blob and blob-stream; they are not the recipe producer.

cores.label: `cores/pong` simulation
cores.router: No place-and-route producer. `make sim-pong` simulates this module.
cores.quartus: No Quartus flow for this module.
cores.features: Not a package. No media, input, HDMI or mesh contract of its own. The package is `fes.pong`.
cores.notes: `sources/misteross/docs/cores.md` says `cores/pong` is the standalone Pong game module and is not a package.
cores.oss_note: No toolchain lock. This directory is not a bitstream.

cores.label: `fes.pcxt`
cores.router: Diagnostic producer authenticates its own lock and accepts `PCXT_GPU_ROUTER` HIP or CUDA (`cores/fes-pcxt/README.md`). Not a recipe row, so there is no recipe `gpu_router`.
cores.quartus: Quartus 17.0.2 is a cross-check, not the producer. The CGA Direct build from the old nextpnr timer failed that cross-check and is not timing-qualified (core README, issue #840). There is no automatic Quartus fallback. Calling Quartus the primary product toolchain is unverified.
cores.features: Media: diagnostic firmware byte port only. No disk controller and no sealed firmware map. Input: no HID keyboard frontend. HDMI: diagnostic 720p RGB on the DE10-Nano shell (CGA or MDA, Direct or Scanlines). No runtime ABI. Mesh/Bluetooth: per-core unverified (host evdev and FogCast only).
cores.notes: Unregistered. No `config/core-recipes.toml` row and no package. Cannot boot DOS. SDRAM pad timing and hardware remain unqualified in the core README.

cores.label: `fes.pc386`
cores.router: Machine synthesis packs with nextpnr-mistral and does not route (`scripts/synth_fes_pc386.py`). The default lock is the i386 lock. Not a recipe row.
cores.quartus: No Quartus producer for the machine was found. The machine design sketches `scripts/build_fes_pc386_oss.py`, which is not in the tree. Calling Quartus the primary product toolchain is unverified.
cores.features: Media: ATA disk in host simulation only. Input: PS/2 keyboard and mouse models; the README says the HID row model and typematic repeat are not built yet. HDMI: 720p presenter and display plane in simulation. Audio: OPL2 and Sound Blaster in simulation. No shell, package or kit evidence. Mesh/Bluetooth: per-core unverified (host evdev and FogCast only).
cores.notes: Host-only machine (phases M1–M3) plus diagnostic Cyclone V synthesis. Not a catalog package. CPU is `fes_i386_cpu`, with the Bochs oracle standing in for the CPU in the machine simulation.

cores.label: `fes_i386_cpu`
cores.router: CPU timing spikes use this lock with the GPU router. Not a package producer and not a recipe row.
cores.quartus: Quartus 17.0.2 fits the same Yosys netlist as an oracle (`scripts/quartus_fes_i386.py`). The far-transfer record is about 69–74 MHz nextpnr and about 98–104 MHz Quartus. Accepted policy would ship both labelled builds once the 15% rule is met; recipe and package selection for that are not implemented. A gap that only nextpnr shows is filed on the flow (DeanoC/nextpnr#300, `docs/i386-cpu-design.md`). Calling Quartus the primary product toolchain is unverified.
cores.features: Not a system package. No media, HDMI, Bluetooth or mesh of its own. Phase 1 real-mode pipeline is in progress in the CPU design doc. The pc386 machine is the intended consumer and does not yet seal a package.
cores.notes: Shared CPU RTL. Device `5CSEBA6U23I7` in the spike harness. Yosys pin `238eac9a` is newer than the repository lock's `3a5accbd` and is scoped to this CPU.

cores.label: `fes_z80_nmos` / `fes_z80_fast`
cores.router: No place-and-route producer. Consumers authenticate their own locks.
cores.quartus: No Quartus flow for the shared CPU. ZX81, Coleco, SMS and RAM Tester have their own oracle targets.
cores.features: Not a system package. `fes_z80_nmos` is the product CPU for ZX81 (and the ZX80/TS models), SG-1000 and the Spectrum models. No product core selects `fes_z80_fast`. Coleco and SMS still instantiate TV80.
cores.notes: Shared RTL under `cores/fes-common/rtl/z80`. No toolchain lock of its own. Each consumer needs its own timing and hardware qualification.
cores.oss_note: No bitstream and no toolchain lock of its own.

cores.label: `cpu6502`

cores.features: Not a system package. Verilog NMOS 6502 used by Apple II, C64 and the development 1541.
cores.notes: Imported Arlet `verilog-6502` with the local rename and SO-pin changes in its README. No toolchain lock of its own.
cores.oss_note: No bitstream and no toolchain lock of its own.

cores.label: `fx68k`
cores.router: No place-and-route producer. Atari ST authenticates its own lock.
cores.quartus: No Quartus flow for this CPU.
cores.features: Not a system package. Motorola 68000 used by `fes.atari-st`.
cores.notes: FX68K by Jorge Cwik, GPL-3.0-or-later, no local RTL changes recorded in its README. No toolchain lock of its own.
cores.oss_note: No bitstream and no toolchain lock of its own.

cores.label: TV80
cores.router: No place-and-route producer. Coleco and SMS authenticate their own locks.
cores.quartus: No separate Quartus flow. Coleco and SMS oracles build those machines, not this CPU alone.
cores.features: Not a system package. Historical Z80 still instantiated by Coleco and SMS. Not `fes_z80_nmos`.
cores.notes: Core alignment lists TV80/T80 as the remaining divergence from the first-party NMOS Z80. No toolchain lock of its own.
cores.oss_note: No bitstream and no toolchain lock of its own.

unverified.detail: A Tier 1 of "HIL-verified on kits and present in the default image" has no matching playable core. The bootstrap image is `fes.menu` plus the pinned splash. Catalog `supported` is what this page calls Tier 1. Whether any of those cores should move to a stricter current-byte HIL tier is open.

The request to treat Quartus as primary, and nextpnr builds as advisory with misses filed as nextpnr issues, is not how the tree labels these blocks. i386 already files nextpnr-only gaps on DeanoC/nextpnr#300, and its Quartus fit stays an oracle until the variant rollout lands. pc386 has no producer. PC/XT's producer is OSS. The primary-toolchain cell is unverified.

"Old media handling (0 titles)" and "low priority" were not found as statements. The factory package strips blob and blob-stream. The arcade room hardcodes five cabinet names and shows `no Coleco arcade titles in this library yet` when none of them are installed. No committed title catalog with a count of 0 was found, and no priority ranking was found.
Their recipes say `bring-up/check oracle`, and the only Quartus make target found for that shell is `build-fes-zx81-quartus`. Coverage of the other three models is unverified.

On this tree there is no sources/misteross/boards/de25nano directory, and no per-core Agilex 5 constraints, pins or image. The cell is the board-wide policy plus TBD, not a port plan. Open pull requests that are not on this branch add that directory and Quartus diagnostics (board metadata #1176, idle and menu scanout #1201, ZX81 BASIC and HDMI #1229, plus follow-ups). The checker fails when boards/de25nano appears, so those rows have to be rewritten from the merged tree.

unverified.where: Every row with a pad or keyboard
unverified.detail: Bluetooth HID/HoG pairing is a host evdev path in the FogCast README. No per-core Bluetooth interface was found.
Launch, library and mesh are host services. No per-core mesh capability flag was found, so this page does not claim that any core is in or out of the mesh.

No recipe records a completed OSS-versus-Quartus sign-off comparison against the 15% rule. i386 is the named example and is not a registered core. Which current cores would qualify to ship a Quartus variant is unverified.

Core status and the validation notes bind acceptance to named packages. This matrix does not copy those package ids forward. Which rows Deano wants marked HIL-verified for the bytes in the tree is open.
